metaDescription: Seven 1.7 liter electric kettles compared on wattage, presets, glass versus stainless and lid design, for families that boil several mugs at once.
expertTake: The Cosori 1.7L with temperature control is the best all-rounder, with 1500 W, five presets and a lid that opens two ways. The Cosori plain 1.7L is the pick for buyers who just want a wide mouth and a fast boil. If you boil for one person, a 1.7 liter kettle is more than you need.
introParagraphs: Seventeen hundred milliliters is the standard family kettle size. It fills about seven cups, covers a pot of tea for a table, and is the capacity most manufacturers use for their full-featured models. Almost every model at this size runs at or near the maximum a household outlet allows.

That makes wattage a poor way to separate them. The differences are in body material, temperature control, lid geometry and how much plastic the water touches. This guide compares glass, stainless and double-wall designs so you can match a kettle to the way you actually use it.

products.name: Cosori 1.7L stainless kettle with 5 presets and 1500W

specList.label: Presets
specList.value: Boil, black, oolong, green and more

products.description:
This is the full-featured Cosori. That 1500 watt element heats a 304 stainless all-metal interior, and five one-touch presets cover boil, black tea, oolong, green tea and one more setting. The temperature accuracy is listed at within 5 degrees Fahrenheit, which is good for a consumer kettle.

Two lid angles solve a problem most kettles ignore. A small opening cuts splash while you check the water, and the wide opening gives access for cleaning and refilling. Against the plain Cosori below, you pay for presets and keep the same wide-mouth philosophy.

The plastic-free interior is the feature that justifies the choice over the Elite Gourmet, which uses a double wall but does not make the same claim in the data. Expect to descale every few weeks in hard water. It is the kettle to buy if you want one device for tea, coffee and quick boils.
products.bestFor: Households that brew different teas and coffee from one kettle.
pros: 1500 W element for a full 1.7 L boil
All-metal interior with no plastic contact
cons: Controls add cost over a plain boiler

products.name: Cosori 1.7L stainless kettle, plastic-free, wide opening
products.description:
Cosori's plain model skips the presets and keeps what makes the brand good. The stated claim is that 0.5 liters of water heats in under three minutes, which is the practical number for a morning mug or two. The wide mouth and large-angle lid let a hand reach every corner for cleaning.

The listing also says water never touches plastic, which makes it a rare combination of simple controls and a clean water path. Against the Hamilton Beach glass kettle, you give up the visible water but gain a stainless interior and a sturdier body. Against the temperature-control Cosori, you save on features you may never use.

Upkeep is easy because the wide mouth invites a regular wipe. In hard water, descale monthly. It suits buyers who want a kettle that behaves the same on day one and day one thousand.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want easy cleaning and a plastic-free path without presets.
pros: Wide mouth and large-angle lid for cleaning
Stated 0.5 L boil in under three minutes
No plastic contact per the listing
cons: No view of the water level through the body

products.name: Elite Gourmet 1.7L double-wall touchscreen kettle, 1100W
products.description:
Elite Gourmet fits a real-time display and a touchscreen on a double-wall kettle. Four preset temperatures can be nudged in 5 degree steps, which is finer control than most presets allow. A keep-warm mode holds the temperature for up to two hours, with auto shut-off and boil-dry protection.

The element is 1100 watts, lower than the 1500 watt kettles in this guide, so a full fill takes longer. That is the compromise for a quieter draw on the circuit and a cool body. The listing describes a 304 stainless interior and borosilicate glass elements.

Compared with the COMFEE glass kettle, it trades the visible water for a cooler shell and a display. Expect to wait around seven to eight minutes for a full boil. Consider it a good pick if you want to see the temperature and hold it for a long breakfast.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a digital readout and a long keep-warm.
pros: Keep warm for up to 2 hours
Double wall for a cooler shell
cons: 1100 W boils slower than 1500 W rivals
Touchscreen adds parts that can fail

products.name: COMFEE' 1.7L glass kettle with 6 presets and 2-hour keep warm
products.description:
COMFEE combines a glass body with a 1500 watt element and six preset temperatures. A two-hour keep-warm mode and an LED indicator make it straightforward, and the base uses 304 food-grade stainless steel. It targets tea drinkers who also want to see their water.

The glass is the point of difference from the Cosori. You can watch the boil and spot scale early, but the surface gets hot and can break if knocked. Six presets give it more range than the four on the Elite Gourmet, at a higher wattage.

In ownership, clean the glass with vinegar when it clouds and keep it away from edges. The stainless base is the part to descale, since scale forms there first. Reach for it as a good fit for a tea shelf rather than a rough family kitchen.
products.bestFor: Tea drinkers who want presets and a clear view of the water.
pros: 1500 W for a quick full boil
Glass body shows water and scale
cons: Glass surface gets hot to touch
Breakable if knocked on a counter edge

products.name: Cuisinart JK-17P1 1.7L cordless kettle, 1500W
products.description:
Cuisinart's JK-17P1 is the everyday kettle without extras. Its 1500 watt element heats 1.7 liters, a backlit blue water window shows the level, and the kettle lifts off a 360 degree swivel base so left- and right-handed users can set it either way. The handle is nonslip and stays cool.

There are no presets, so it boils and stops. That makes it the fair comparison for the Hamilton Beach glass model, with a stainless body and a window instead of a clear glass body. Next to the Cosori, the window and the base are the draw.

The cordless design is the best part of ownership, as it lifts and pours without trailing a lead. Wipe the window area and descale every month. It is a reliable choice for homes that want predictable, no-menu operation.
products.bestFor: Households that want a plain, familiar kettle with a clear water window.
pros: Backlit water window with level markings
cons: Single wall shell can get hot

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1.7L glass kettle, 1500W
products.description:
Hamilton Beach sells this as a straightforward glass kettle with a 1500 watt element. The maker says it boils up to 1.7 liters faster than a microwave, and the interior is borosilicate glass that is BPA-free. It switches off automatically when the water reaches a boil.

It is a no-frills choice that sits in the lower price tier of this lineup. The cordless design makes pouring easy and the glass shows the boil. The compromise is the same as any glass kettle: the shell gets hot and scale is visible.

Use it for water, not milk or soup, and descale when clouding appears. For a family on a budget that likes seeing the water, it is a sound option.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a glass kettle for daily water.

products.name: Yoochu 1.7L double-wall stainless kettle, 1500W
products.description:
Yoochu built this as a family kettle with an anti-scald double wall. The listing says it brings 1.7 liters to a full 212 degree boil in about six minutes at 1500 watts, and that every water-contact surface, including the spout and the lid, is 304 stainless steel. Insulation also keeps water hot longer.

That makes it a close match to the Cosori plain model on materials, with the added double wall. The compromise is a narrower opening than the Cosori's wide mouth, so cleaning is by soak rather than by hand.

Ownership is simple: fill, boil, pour, empty. Descale monthly. If you share a kitchen with young children, the cool shell is the reason to choose it over the glass kettles.
products.bestFor: Family kitchens that need a cool shell and stainless water contact.
pros: 1500 W with a stated six minute boil
304 stainless on lid, spout and interior

buyingCriteria.criterion: Boil speed for a full pot
buyingCriteria.explanation: Boiling 1.7 liters from cold needs roughly 570 kilojoules, so a 1500 W element needs about eight minutes in theory and six to seven in practice with insulation. The Yoochu lists six minutes and the Elite Gourmet at 1100 W will take noticeably longer. Check wattage rather than marketing claims when time matters. Boil time also stretches in winter, when tap water starts colder, so a kettle that feels slow in January is not necessarily failing.

The Cosori with temperature control has five presets, the COMFEE has six and the Elite Gourmet has four adjustable ones. Green tea at 175 degrees and black tea near boiling taste different. If you drink one type, you do not need many presets, but if you brew several, they save guesswork.

The COMFEE and Hamilton Beach use glass, the Cosori, Yoochu and Elite Gourmet use stainless. Glass shows the water and scale, while stainless is tougher and hides both. Choose based on whether you value visibility or durability.

The temperature-control Cosori offers two lid angles, which reduces splash and opens wide for cleaning. A standard lid forces a compromise. If you refill at the tap with one hand, a hinge that stays open is worth more than a spec on the box.

The Elite Gourmet and COMFEE hold temperature for up to two hours, and the Cosori with presets has a hold function. Keep-warm is useful for a long breakfast but draws idle power. Skip it if you drain the kettle straight away. A two hour hold on a kettle that you refill at breakfast and again at lunch means the element cycles on and off for hours, so treat it as a convenience for hosting rather than a default setting.

The Cosori, Yoochu and the Elite Gourmet list stainless interiors and some also list stainless lids. A kettle with a plastic underside on the lid will carry warm plastic into your tea. Read what the lid and spout are made of before trusting a body claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity purity
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept kettles listed at 1.7 L and left out 1.5 and 2 L models. This keeps the comparison on boil time fair. The Yoochu lists 1.7 L as 8 cups.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed and wattage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated wattage and boil time. Most picks are 1500 W, with the Elite Gourmet at 1100 W as the outlier. The Yoochu's six minute claim and the Cosori's under three minutes for 0.5 L are the clearest figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control depth
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed presets, accuracy and keep-warm. The Cosori with presets and the COMFEE lead here, while the Cuisinart JK-17P1 and Hamilton Beach have none. Controls only count if they work reliably.

howWeEvaluated.title: Body material and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared glass, stainless and double-wall shells. The Yoochu and Elite Gourmet score well for cool exteriors, and the glass kettles lose points for hot surfaces. Safety cutouts are present on every pick.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at lid openings and interior access. The Cosori wide mouth and two lid angles lead, with glass making scale visible on the COMFEE and Hamilton Beach. Narrow stainless neck kettles are harder to clean by hand.

rows: Family with mixed tea and coffee
Double wall at a moderate cost

cards.label: Glass
cards.text: The COMFEE and Hamilton Beach show the water and have no metal taste. They get hot and can break, and scale shows clearly. They suit careful households.

cards.label: Stainless
cards.text: The Cosori models, Yoochu and Elite Gourmet are durable and quiet to handle. Double-wall versions stay cool, though scale hides. They suit busy kitchens.

howToChoose.note: Choose glass for visibility, stainless for rough use.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least four presets covering 175 to 212 degrees, a hold function and a stainless or glass water path. Delicate teas brew best well below boiling.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Cosori 1.7L with presets, COMFEE 1.7L and Elite Gourmet 1.7L all offer presets. The Cosori adds the tightest stated accuracy.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You brew several types of tea or coffee. The Cosori with presets and the Elite Gourmet's fine adjustment pay for themselves in better cups.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need boiling water. The Hamilton Beach 1.7L and Cuisinart JK-17P1 both do that with 1500 W and an auto shut-off.

maintenance.why: Scale coats the element and slows the boil. A citric acid soak clears it in one cycle.
Clouding hides the water level. A vinegar rinse restores the view.
Steam residue builds at hinges and can make lids stick. A soft brush helps.
Water on the contacts can corrode them. Dry before reconnecting.
On digital models, a flickering display can hint at moisture inside. Keep steam away from the touch area.

faq.q: Is 1.7 L too large for one person?
faq.a: For most solo users, yes. It heats more water than you need and takes longer to boil a small amount. Fill only to the amount you need.

faq.q: How long does a 1.7 L kettle take to boil?
faq.a: About six to eight minutes for a full fill at 1500 W. The Yoochu lists six minutes. An 1100 W kettle will take longer.

faq.q: Do presets make tea taste better?
faq.a: For green and white tea, yes, because boiling water extracts bitterness. Black tea is fine at boiling. Presets matter less for coffee in a plunger.

faq.q: Which is safer for kids, glass or double wall?
faq.a: Double wall. The outer shell stays cool, while glass gets as hot as the water. Always keep the spout away from small hands.

faq.q: Can I boil anything other than water?
faq.a: No. Milk, soup and noodles foam up, burn on the element and damage the kettle. Use water only. Adding tea leaves directly to a kettle without an infuser also clogs the spout filter, so brew in a pot or mug.

faq.q: Why does my kettle click off late?
faq.a: Scale can insulate the sensor. Descale and wipe the steam tube, and check the lid is closed firmly.
